game: Exolon / Exolon New! (Sharp MZ-800, Datelsoft conversion)
author: Original game: Raffaele Cecco; original music: Nick Jones. Sharp conversion credited to DATELSOFT in the preserved program.

source.memory: 64KB loader snapshot immediately before original entry $6d60. MZF body is loaded at $3960, relocated backwards to $6960–$ffff; $6d4b copies $0400 bytes from $6960 to $3000 and runs original setup. Source contains the original converted routines, not a replacement Spectrum sound bank.
source.catalogLimit: MZPico identifies Datelsoft and a Spectrum port; its bootstrap metadata is explicitly uncurated. No claim of an official Hewson Sharp release or a pristine commercial master is made.

extraction.psgWriter: $b758 silences all four SN76489 channels through port $f2. Patched effect writers $c097/$c0b1/$c0cc write SN attenuation bytes, then call the original Datelsoft converter $332f to emit the two tone-period bytes. Music writes the same chip directly. Capture preserves every port byte, including repeated mute writes.

clock.description: Sharp service manual clock diagram: 17.7344MHz PAL master divided by five. MAME also identifies the MZ-800 PSG as SN76489A at PAL master/5; its 17.734470MHz crystal value differs by about four parts per million.

extraction.timing: Original effect programs advanced at 50 driver steps/second, original title program at 90 steps/second, matching the existing native-game presentation convention. These are isolated captures: the original conversion calls the title update after four text-render calls and effects in a variable-duration game loop. These recordings preserve converted pitches, note order, attenuation and all chip writes; they do not claim measured original-machine tempo. Instruction T-states locate writes within each step; no video wait states or contention are modeled.
extraction.traceFormat: MZ8SN001: 8-byte ASCII magic, little-endian uint32 duration in microseconds and uint32 event count; each 8-byte event is uint32 timestamp, uint8 F2 output value and three zero reserved bytes.

offlineRenderer.license: MIT; external offline tool only, not redistributed or loaded by the game
offlineRenderer.psg: Independent SN76489A renderer: 10-bit square-wave periods, clock/16 counter ticks, zero period treated as 1024, 2dB attenuation steps and volume15 silence. It integrates chip transitions over PCM sample intervals, then applies 20Hz AC coupling. Noise uses SN76489A feedback; all original captured Exolon programs keep the SN noise channel muted. The converted routines do not retain the original AY noise channel, and this capture does not invent one.
offlineRenderer.output: Mono PCM16 WAV at 44100Hz. Software rendering, not a microphone or physical-hardware recording.

extraction.reproducePcmWithoutCpu: Copy audio-engine.bin, sn-tone-converter.bin and *.snr into an output directory, then node --experimental-strip-types tools/audio/sharp.mjs --traces-only --output /tmp/exolon-sharp-audio

shot.evidence: Ammo $8e5a is decremented immediately before the call at $836b–$8371. First sounding port bytes are $92,$83,$38, exactly from the Sharp driver.

grenade.evidence: Original initializer allocates simultaneous slots9 and15; capture retains both SN tone voices.

refill-ammo.evidence: Ammo set to99 at $9978–$997c immediately before sound.

refill-grenades.evidence: Grenades set to10 at $99ce–$99d2 immediately before sound.

suit.evidence: Changing chamber toggles suit state $9ed8, then calls the same routine as ammo refill.

adaptationAliases.death: Presentation alias to original explosion $c148; no distinct original Sharp player-death program is claimed.
adaptationAliases.suit: Identical to refill-ammo, following original $9f65 call.

limits: Dedicated Sharp sound bank over the shared native TypeScript game model. No CPU emulator, MZF program or SN renderer runs in the browser: it loads the pre-rendered WAV files. Concurrent voice allocation and interruption are isolated per sound. No separate Sharp game-over recording is claimed. The earlier Spectrum, C64, CPC, Game Boy and arranged recordings are retained.
